description: Regression cases for DSH/FastCtx tool routing, PTC SDK orchestration, CLI selection, programming quality, and engineering tradeoffs.

cases.input: Read three known local source files before a change.
expected: Use one FastCtx inspect_local_file call with files array
Do not shell-cat each file separately

cases.input: Find all occurrences of a plain-text feature flag in src.
expected: Use FastCtx grep or rg with scoped path/glob
Do not read the entire repository

cases.input: Find TypeScript calls with a specific AST shape.
expected: Load ast-grep skill
Use sg pattern matching
Test positive and negative examples

cases.input: Find callers and impact of AuthService.refresh.
expected: Load codebase-memory skill
Query symbol/call relationships
Cross-check current source

cases.input: Rename a plain-text token across many files.
expected: Use FastCtx replace dry-run or sd preview
Check encoding, line endings, match count and diff

cases.input: Two independent read-only module investigations.
expected: Run in parallel in one batch when tool limits permit
Avoid duplicate output and oversized context

cases.input: Two tasks both need to edit src/auth.ts.
expected: Serialize writes
Define one writer or split non-overlapping edits

cases.input: A shell command may take six minutes.
expected: Use FastCtx run_background
Track with job_list/job_output
Do not wait in foreground

cases.input: Use GitHub plugin to edit a repository, but no GitHub plugin is registered.
expected: Do not assume GitHub plugin exists
Use authenticated git/API only if available
Otherwise report remote-write blocker

cases.input: Look up latest API usage, but no Context7 plugin is registered.
expected: Do not call invented Context7 tools
Check version lockfile and official docs
State any unverified API behavior

cases.input: FastCtx result ends with Partial and includes continuation parameters.
expected: Continue using the exact returned parameters
Stop when Complete

cases.input: A non-idempotent publish command returns an error.
expected: Inspect remote state before retry
Do not blindly repeat the side effect

cases.input: Change one known line in one known file.
expected: Use direct edit
Do not spawn a subagent or create a heavyweight plan

cases.input: Implement a multi-module feature with shared interfaces.
expected: Clarify requirements and define interfaces/plan first
Parallelize only independent work after boundaries are stable

cases.input: Code edits completed but tests were not run.
expected: Do not report tests as passed
Report implementation and verification limitation separately

cases.input: Need multiple independent facts from the same API source.
expected: Use one batch request if supported
Do not create unnecessary parallel calls

cases.input: Search compressed zstd JSONL logs.
expected: Use rg -z or zstd -d -c pipeline when format confirmed
Avoid unnecessary full extraction to disk

cases.input: MCP tool is absent, but a baked mcp2cli adapter may exist.
expected: Check actual adapter availability/help
Use only for known baked MCPs
Otherwise choose an alternative or report blocker

cases.input: In a DSH PTC session, combine multiple registered tools in one TypeScript program.
expected: Use the injected tools:sdk namespace through run_code
Read actual generated tool names and argument schemas
Keep intermediate values inside the program and return only the needed result

cases.input: Use Promise.all for multiple PTC tool bindings where some tools may be exclusive.
expected: Do not assume Promise.all guarantees execution overlap
Only concurrency-safe calls may overlap; exclusive calls remain barriers
Respect maxParallelSubCalls

cases.input: A PTC program performs a write and a later tool call fails.
expected: Catch or report ToolCallError with toolName where possible
Do not assume previous side effects were rolled back
Inspect actual state before retrying non-idempotent operations

cases.input: The active session is not PTC and no tools:sdk section is exposed.
expected: Do not fabricate the PTC SDK
Use available native tools or the actual active execution mode
Do not pretend PTC execution occurred

cases.input: Find every call site of a symbol across modules and identify blast radius.
expected: Use codebase-memory for symbols/call graph/impact analysis
Cross-check with current source using FastCtx/rg/sg
Do not rely on text search alone

cases.input: Search TypeScript files when paths may contain spaces or newlines.
expected: Use fd -0 with xargs -0 or an equivalent NUL-safe pipeline
Avoid unquoted command substitution

cases.input: Compare a large refactor diff structurally.
expected: Use difft for structural code diff when available
Use delta only for Git diff presentation
Do not confuse formatting with semantic verification

cases.input: Check whether a required CLI tool is installed.
expected: Use command -v or git-which
Do not assume aliases exist in non-interactive scripts
Do not install dependencies silently

cases.input: Refactor a small duplicate expression in two places.
expected: Apply KISS and DRY judgment
Do not create a new abstraction unless shared knowledge is stable and there is real reuse value

cases.input: Optimize a slow code path.
expected: Measure/profile before editing
Use Amdahl's law to prioritize the dominant cost
Verify performance with representative data

cases.input: Change a public function whose callers rely on its current ordering and error behavior.
expected: Apply Hyrum's law and inspect observable behavior/callers
Treat compatibility and migration as explicit design constraints
Add regression tests

cases.input: Design a new system with many speculative extension points.
expected: Apply Gall's law, Worse is Better, YAGNI and second-system-effect checks
Start with a simple working core and evolve from demonstrated requirements

cases.input: Implement a function that handles IO, business rules, and formatting.
expected: Apply SRP, separation of concerns, single abstraction level
Keep IO at boundaries and business logic testable

cases.input: Add concurrency to a batch operation.
expected: Check idempotency, shared mutable state, cancellation and concurrency limits
Parallelize only independent concurrency-safe operations
Serialize writes to shared resources

cases.input: Decide whether to introduce an interface and dependency injection.
expected: Apply interface programming and SOLID based on actual substitution/testing boundaries
Do not create interfaces for every single implementation by default

cases.input: Handle untrusted external API input and internal validated domain values.
expected: Validate and normalize at external boundaries
Fail fast on internal contract violations
Do not duplicate defensive checks throughout trusted internal layers

cases.input: Choose between adding configuration options and using a default convention.
expected: Apply convention over configuration for common paths
Expose configuration only for real user-controlled variation
Preserve least-surprise defaults

cases.input: A module duplicates a value that is also maintained in a schema and generated config.
expected: Apply single source of truth
Generate or reference derived values rather than maintaining duplicate authorities

cases.input: Separate a state-changing operation from a query.
expected: Use CQRS/command-query separation at the method/API boundary where useful
Avoid introducing a full CQRS architecture without demonstrated need

cases.input: Choose a design from many proposed patterns.
expected: Use first-principles constraints, Occam and Pareto
Choose the simplest design that meets correctness, safety and operational requirements

cases.input: A code task has a nearby known serious quality issue and many unrelated style issues.
expected: Fix relevant high-impact nearby issues
Avoid unrelated broad cleanup that expands the diff

cases.input: A cross-module design introduces a new storage model and deployment dependency.
expected: Record a short ADR
Document alternatives, rationale, risks, rollback and verification
